annotations.text:
The underlined headers are gone.

A section head is now a big serif title, a condensed caps meta beside it, and a link pushed right — separation comes from space and from the content below being a real object.

This departs from DECISIONS 2026-09-04 ("a serif title over a 2px ink rule with flat content beneath"), which is still what League Home does. Worth deciding whether the rule changes everywhere or the home screen is the exception.

Where the colour comes from now:

• Club crests blown up to 168px and bled off the top-right of each league card at 7% — depth without a shadow or a gradient.
• Real PL badges at 24px in every fixture row.
• Player cut-outs on plinths coloured by the player's own tactical role, so the twelve-position spine does visual work instead of sitting in a chip.
• One dark green block near the foot, so the page has a floor and the cream is not unbroken top to bottom.

Top Rated is portraits now.

Mobile swipes a rail of four at 132px; desktop lays six across the full 1180 at 208px tall with the rank in the corner. Same data, composed for the width rather than reflowed.

Sourced at 500x500 from the PL photo CDN and downsampled to 240px, so they hold up at desktop size — the earlier 110x140 crops did not.

The two breakpoints are composed separately, not reflowed.

Mobile: one column, league cards stacked full width, portraits on a swipe rail, fixtures as full-width rows, 44px targets throughout.

Desktop: leagues take two thirds with the pre-draft card and both doors in a rail beside them; the portrait row then runs the full width as its own band; fixtures split into two columns with the green block alongside. Nothing is a stretched phone layout.

First run: the argument, made with faces.

Matchweek 3 really did finish with Alisson 6th and Haaland 12th of 654 rated players. Both portraits are the actual players — an earlier draft had the wrong faces under those names.
